newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees solid U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees solid U.S. growth.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Thursday that he sees continued solid U.S. economic growth.
Asked about the drop in August U.S. factory orders, Rubin replied, "I don't think that week-to-week numbers or month-to-month numbers say very much of anything."
"I think we very much continue on the same path, solid growth and low inflation," he said.
Rubin said second quarter Gross Domestic Product growth was "very high," and that the third quarter growth is projected to be lower.

"I think if you want to look out over the next six months or the next year or some meaningful period of time, I think far and away the most likely scenario is continuation of solid growth, obviously not at the same level as the second quarter," Rubin said.
He added that he sees continuation of solid growth, low unemployment and low inflation.
